title: Small hypercover generators for local quasi-isomorphisms
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category equipped with a Grothendieck topology by covering sieves: sieves are sets of arrows into an object closed under precomposition, the maximal sieve covers, and covers satisfy pullback stability and transitivity. No fibre products or subcanonicity are assumed. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}_\Lambda)$ with objectwise kernels and cokernels. Use [def-weil-size-convention], cochains and quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], module-presheaf sheafification $\#$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and the enhanced localization $\mathbf D(\mathcal P)$ at objectwise quasi-isomorphisms, with its coherent mapping spaces and colimits [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Presentable means accessible and admitting all small colimits, in the sense of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category].

Put $h_T(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,T)$ and $L_T(V)=\Lambda[h_T(V)]$, the free $\Lambda$-module on this set. A hypercover $U_\bullet\to h_T$ is an augmented simplicial presheaf of sets, each $U_n=\coprod_\alpha h_{S_{n,\alpha}}$, such that the maps to all augmented matching presheaves are epimorphisms after sheafification; the degree-zero matching presheaf is $h_T$ and higher matching presheaves parametrize compatible proper faces. All matching objects are formed in presheaves. Define $A_U^{-n}=\bigoplus_\alpha L_{S_{n,\alpha}}$ for $n\ge0$, $A_U^r=0$ for $r>0$, and its differential for $n\ge1$ by the alternating sum of the face maps. Let $e_U:A_U\to L_T[0]$ be the augmentation. For a complex map $f:P\to Q$, let local quasi-isomorphism mean that $(T\mapsto H^r(f(T)))^\#$ is an isomorphism for every integer $r$.

The infinity category $\mathbf D(\mathcal P)$ is presentable. There is a small set $\mathcal H_0$ of such hypercovers, allowing varying targets, such that if $S=\{e_U[k]:U\in\mathcal H_0,\ k\in\mathbf Z\}$ is regarded as a set of arrows in $\mathbf D(\mathcal P)$, then for every map $f$ of complexes,
$$f\text{ is a local quasi-isomorphism}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad [f]\in\langle S\rangle.$$
Here $\langle S\rangle$ is the smallest class of arrows containing $S$ and equivalences and closed under two-out-of-three, retracts, pushouts and small colimits in the arrow infinity category; arrow colimits are computed on source and target. Every augmentation $e_U$ for any hypercover, including those outside $\mathcal H_0$, is a local quasi-isomorphism. No boundedness on $P,Q$ is assumed.

source.place: Choudhury--Gallauer Alves de Souza, Homotopy theory of dg sheaves, arXiv:1511.02828v1, Facts 5.2 and 5.5, Theorem 5.7(1)-(2), Theorem 5.11 and its proof, printed pp. 17-21; saturation formulation after passing from the projective dg model to its enhanced localization. Presentability follows from Corollary 3.1 and combinatorial localization; the formulation uses the strong-saturation convention of lem-coef-infinity-small-localization-saturation. Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag in the supplied DAG states this enhanced result.

proof.text: Use [lem-cbc-dg-presheaf-model-localizations] to give the unbounded complexes in $\mathcal P$ their combinatorial projective model $\mathsf M$, with weak equivalences exactly the objectwise quasi-isomorphisms. Its coherent localization is therefore the $\mathbf D(\mathcal P)$ specified in the statement, by the same localization universal property. Apply [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability] to $\mathsf M$: it is locally presentable and both model factorization systems are generated by sets, precisely the hypotheses of that theorem. It follows that $\mathbf D(\mathcal P)$ is presentable; no boundedness of its complexes is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 3.1, combined with the existing combinatorial-model presentability theorem.

proof.text: Choose the small dense set $\mathcal H_0$ given by [lem-cbc-dense-hypercover-set]. Density means a refinement over the same target for every hypercover; it requires neither representable fibre products nor subcanonicity. Because the targets range over the small category and $\mathbf Z$ is small, $B=\{e_U[k]:U\in\mathcal H_0,\ k\in\mathbf Z\}$ is a small set of actual complex maps. Its image in $\mathbf D(\mathcal P)$ is the set $S$ in the statement.

source.place: Fact 5.2; dense-set terminology in DHI Definition 6.1.

proof.text: Fix any hypercover $U\to h_T$, not necessarily in $\mathcal H_0$. Its matching epimorphisms give local lifts of every matching section by [lem-cbc-presheaf-sheafification-epi-local-lifts]. Here is the finite coning argument, with augmented homological degree $-1$ denoting $h_T$. A cycle in the augmented free chain complex over an object $V$ is a finite linear combination of simplices. Keep the finite diagram of these simplices and all their iterated faces, with the original simplices as labels. First, for each target arrow $t:V\to T$ occurring in this diagram, locally choose a vertex $c(t)$ over $t$. Inductively, when cones of all lower-dimensional faces have been chosen, prescribe the faces of a cone on an $n$-simplex $\sigma$ by $d_0c(\sigma)=\sigma$ and $d_{i+1}c(\sigma)=c(d_i\sigma)$ for $0\le i\le n$. They form a compatible matching section: the relations with $d_0$ use the previously prescribed $d_0c(d_i\sigma)=d_i\sigma$, and the remaining relations use the simplicial identities on $\sigma$. The matching-map local lifting criterion supplies $c(\sigma)$ on a further covering sieve. Only finitely many choices are made in each finite diagram, so intersections of covering sieves and their transitivity supply a common covering refinement. Extend $c$ linearly on the original finite labelled diagram. The formula $\partial c(\sigma)=\sigma-c(\partial\sigma)$ follows by separating the $d_0$ term in the alternating sum, also in degree zero with $c(\partial\sigma)$ the chosen vertex over the augmentation. Thus every augmented cycle becomes a boundary locally. Original labels are retained after restriction, even when two sections become equal there; cancellation in the original finite chain diagram then still proves $c(\partial z)=0$. The same initial vertex choice locally lifts an arbitrary finite linear combination of target arrows, so the augmentation is locally surjective as well.

source.place: Agent proof by finite cones from the hypercover matching condition; no point or representable-intersection argument.

proof.text: Let $b:\mathcal P\to\mathcal A$ be the exact module-sheafification left adjoint of [lem-cbc-sieve-module-sheafification], with fully faithful right adjoint $i$. Every presheaf of homology of the augmented complex in step 3 has every section locally zero. Such a presheaf $E$ has $bE=0$: for any module sheaf $F$, every map $E\to iF$ sends each section to a locally zero section of the sheaf $F$, hence to zero by the sheaf uniqueness axiom; adjunction applied with $F=bE$ makes $\mathrm{id}_{bE}=0$. Exactness of $b$ identifies the homology of the sheafified augmented complex with the sheafification of its homology, since kernels, images and their quotients are preserved. Hence the sheafified augmented complex is exact. Equivalently $H^r(e_U)^\#$ is an isomorphism for every $r$. This proves that every hypercover augmentation is in $W_J$, and reindexing degrees proves the same for every integer shift.

source.document: agent proof: exact sheafification of finite-cone homology
source.place: Agent conclusion of the finite-cone proof using exact module sheafification.

proof.text: Form the projective left Bousfield model $\mathsf M_B$ of [lem-cbc-dg-presheaf-model-localizations]. Its fibrants are exactly the objects local for the maps $B$ tested by the original projective homotopy function complexes. The same lemma supplies the cohomology-sheaf model $\mathsf M_J$. Step 4 shows $B\subset W_J$, so its universal-property clause gives $W_B\subseteq W_J$. We also have $W_{\mathrm{obj}}\subseteq W_B$, since $\mathsf M_B$ is a left Bousfield localization. On simplicial presheaves form the projective localization $\mathsf U(\mathcal C)_{\mathcal H_0}$ as in [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-localization-comparison]; its mapping spaces are projectively derived, so no projective cofibrancy of an arbitrary hypercover is assumed.

source.place: The paragraph before Lemma 5.12 and the first inclusion in the proof of Theorem 5.11; only existence of the cohomology-sheaf model is used.

proof.text: Suppose $q:X\to Y$ is a $\mathsf M_B$-fibration between $\mathsf M_B$-fibrant objects and also belongs to $W_J$. The set $B$ is invariant under every integer shift; by [lem-cbc-dg-presheaf-model-localizations] each $q[k]$ is again a $\mathsf M_B$-fibration between fibrants. Its cohomology sheaf maps are merely reindexed, so $q[k]\in W_J$. The right adjoint $R$ in [lem-cbc-dold-kan-hypercover-quillen] therefore takes $q[k]$ to a fibration between fibrants in $\mathsf U(\mathcal C)_{\mathcal H_0}$ and to a local weak equivalence. Density from step 2 now permits [lem-cbc-simplicial-hypercover-fibration-test]: $R(q[k])$ is an objectwise trivial fibration and in particular has lifts against every representable simplicial boundary inclusion.

source.place: Lemma 5.13, pp. 20-21; DHI arXiv v2 Lemma 6.4 and the projective-model paragraph of Theorem 6.2.

proof.text: The identity from $\mathsf M_B$ back to $\mathsf M$ is right Quillen, so $q$ is an objectwise degreewise surjection by [lem-cbc-dg-presheaf-model-localizations]. Fix $V$ and a cycle $z\in\ker(q(V))^r$. In the shift $X[r]\to Y[r]$, use the two endpoints $0,z$ and the zero interval in $Y[r](V)$ to form the boundary lifting problem. Under the adjunction and the explicit interval identification of [lem-cbc-dold-kan-hypercover-quillen], the lift provided by step 6 is an element $h\in\ker(q(V))^{r-1}$ with $dh=z$ (rescale $h$ by the cochain shift sign if necessary). Thus the kernel is acyclic in every degree. A surjective chain map with acyclic kernel is a quasi-isomorphism: lift a target cycle, kill the differential of the lift by a boundary in the kernel to obtain a source cycle; if a source cycle maps to a target boundary, subtract the differential of any lifted primitive and then a kernel boundary. These two operations prove surjectivity and injectivity on cohomology. Consequently $q\in W_{\mathrm{obj}}\subseteq W_B$. The integer $r$ was arbitrary, so this argument treats unbounded complexes.

source.place: Lemma 5.13, expanded interval lifting and the elementary acyclic-kernel argument.

proof.text: Now take any $f:P\to Q$ in $W_J$. Use the functorial fibrant replacements in $\mathsf M_B$ from [lem-cbc-dg-presheaf-model-localizations] to get a commuting square from $f$ to $f^{\mathrm f}:P^{\mathrm f}\to Q^{\mathrm f}$ whose vertical arrows are in $W_B\subseteq W_J$. Two-out-of-three gives $f^{\mathrm f}\in W_J$. Factor $f^{\mathrm f}=p\circ j$ in $\mathsf M_B$, with $j$ a trivial cofibration and $p$ a fibration. The intermediate object is fibrant because $Q^{\mathrm f}$ is fibrant. Since $j\in W_B\subseteq W_J$, also $p\in W_J$. Steps 6-7 apply to $p$, so $p\in W_B$; then $f^{\mathrm f}\in W_B$ and the replacement square gives $f\in W_B$. Together with step 5 this proves $W_J=W_B$ without assuming that $P$ or $Q$ is fibrant or bounded.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 5.11, expanding the comparison criterion in DHI arXiv v2 Lemma 6.3.

proof.text: By [lem-cbc-dg-presheaf-model-localizations], $f\in W_B$ means exactly that its image $[f]$ induces an equivalence of mapping spaces into every $S$-local object of $\mathbf D(\mathcal P)$: projective homotopy function complexes are its coherent mapping spaces, every complex is projectively fibrant, and the images of $B$ are $S$. Step 1 established presentability and step 2 established smallness, so [lem-coef-infinity-small-localization-saturation] applies and identifies this mapping-space condition with $[f]\in\langle S\rangle$. Its closure operations are exactly equivalences, two-out-of-three, retracts, pushouts and small arrow colimits as required, with arrow colimits computed on source and target. Combine this identification with step 8 to obtain the asserted equivalence for all complex maps. Step 4 already proves the augmentation clause for hypercovers outside $\mathcal H_0$ as well.

source.place: Theorem 5.11, followed by the existing infinity-categorical small-localization saturation theorem.

proof_origin.place: Source-guided proof of Facts 5.2, 5.5 and Theorem 5.11, using Lemmas 5.12-5.13. The two papers are not archived locally; finite-cone exactness is written out independently and the model comparison criterion is expanded.
